_doc: THE SENTENCE LINE (S152, 2026-09-20). Sérgio asked what a 1997 videogame's tool for 'you can press this' would be: Myst's hand cursor and the LucasArts sentence line — nothing in the world glows; a thing NAMES ITSELF when the look rests on it. So: anything pressable in the room says what it is in the caption strip (and the cursor becomes a hand) while the mouse hovers it, the gyro's centre rests on it, or the headset's ray touches it — src/engine/app.ts `aimNameUnderRay`, the same tests in the same order as the press itself. The breath (the lift) stays only for the moment the system points at a thing. Frame voice: plain, lowercase, no charm. The tapes' names come from s1_tapes.json `shelfLabel`; the belongings' from room/belongings.json `label`; the markers' from room/nodes.json `label`.
power: the power button — switch the computer on
racket: the racket on the wall — the first exercise
disk: the companion disk — put it in
boomboxStop: the tape player — stop the tape
_docInst: ⚑ S183 — the institution's corner (src/room/institution.ts). Sérgio, 2026-09-27: 'how can this be more understandable of what they are here? does touching any of them gives added information to the user?' Each object says what it is and what it does to the person, in the frame's plain voice; a press is answered by the object's own movement. 1997 and 2003 are Daniel's file ('your'); 2016 and 2026 are said without a person.
instDrawer: drawer 12 — the file with your name in it
instTerminal: the intake terminal — what you do is typed in here
instReferral: the referral list — the pastor's number, in your mother's pen
instSuitcase: the suitcase — packed for the youth weekend, 12–19 july
instRules: the programme's rules — read, signed, returned
instPacket: the application — twenty-six pages and a liability release
instScanner: the scanner — your paper file becoming a digital one
instRouter: the router — the file travels on a network now
instStatus: a status light — the file is kept somewhere you cannot point to
